title: Tuna Melt
subtitle: Classic tuna and cheese toasted sandwich
excerpt: Tinned tuna mixed with mayonnaise and spring onion, piled onto bread with sliced tomato and Cheddar, then grilled until the cheese bubbles and browns. Simple, fast, satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: The tuna melt is an American diner classic that became popular in British cafes and home kitchens during the 1980s and 1990s. The combination of tinned tuna, mayonnaise, and melted cheese on toast is fast to make and uses store-cupboard ingredients. The cheese should be one that melts readily: Cheddar or Gruyere both work well. Use the grill rather than a sandwich press to get the cheese properly bubbling.

recipeTools.notes: The oven grill or a toaster grill.

content.text: Toast the bread lightly before adding the topping: untoasted bread goes soggy under the wet tuna mixture. Drain the tuna well so the mayo does not become too liquid. Use the grill on high heat so the cheese melts and bubbles without the bread burning.
Heat the grill to high. Toast the bread lightly on both sides.
Mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise, spring onion, lemon juice, and black pepper. Taste and season.
Spread the tuna mixture over 2 slices of toast. Lay the tomato slices on top. Cover generously with grated Cheddar.
Place under the hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and beginning to brown at the edges. Serve immediately.
